headline: At 91, 'Greybeard' Becomes Oldest Person to Finish the Appalachian Trail
meta_description: Dale Sanders, 91, completed the Appalachian Trail thru-hike in 359 days, becoming the oldest person ever to finish the 2,190-mile route.
summary_short: A 91-year-old Kentucky native nicknamed 'Greybeard' has become the oldest person to complete the Appalachian Trail, finishing his second thru-hike on August 31st after 3…
body:
On August 31st at 11:40 p.m., Dale Sanders raised his hands to the sky atop a grey mountaintop in Maine, becoming the oldest person ever to complete a thru-hike of the Appalachian Trail. The 91-year-old, born in Kentucky's backwoods in 1935—before the trail was even finished—accomplished the feat over 359 days and despite 71 falls, including a June hospitalization for a pinched nerve. His route was unconventional: starting from Harper's Ferry, Virginia on September 9th, he first hiked south to Georgia to follow warmer weather, then paused for winter before heading north toward Katahdin, Maine. When his mother-in-law passed away and his injuries mounted, he returned home to Tennessee, but his wife encouraged him to finish. He did, by backtracking through the Great Smoky Mountains and finally reaching Maine.

Sanders had already completed the Appalachian Trail once before, at age 82 in 2017, and recently became the oldest person to finish a rim-to-rim hike of the Grand Canyon. Nicknamed "Greybeard" by supporters for his grey beard and broad sunhat, he credits his success partly to the kindness of "trail angels"—strangers who offered supplies and treats along the way. "When people are taking care of you and bringing you caramel frappes on the trail, the rocks don't matter," he told the Associated Press.

Beyond the record itself lies a philosophy of vitality. Sanders tells the New York Times that the secret is simple: get outside. "I love the outdoors. When I'm in the woods and the Sun is shining, I'm in my best mood." To younger hikers, he offers equally straightforward advice: it's okay to eat doughnuts if you also exercise.
quick_facts: 91-year-old Dale Sanders completed the Appalachian Trail in 359 days
Started September 9th from Harper's Ferry, Virginia; finished August 31st in Maine
Hiked despite 71 falls, a hospitalization, and personal loss
Second thru-hike completion; first was at age 82 in 2017
Born in Kentucky in 1935, before the AT trail was completed
